newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP wants noisy, private Saudi planes out of Europe.
newsitem.headline: EP wants noisy, private Saudi planes out of Europe.

text.p: Euro-MPs called on Tuesday for changes to a European Union directive which exempts noisy, privately owned Saudi Arabian planes from a ban on noisy aircraft using EU airports.
The 1992 directive, 92/14/EEC, outlaws noisy planes built in the 1970s, except those coming from developing countries like Burkina Faso and Uganda.

Dutch Euro-MP Leen van de Waal, who was given the job of examining the European Commission's plans to update the directive, COM(96)413, was astonished to find the list of developing countries also included the oil rich Saudi Arabia.
In addition, he discovered, the exempt Saudi planes were privately owned.
In his report on the proposal, approved by the parliament on Tuesday, van der Waal demanded the annexed list be altered before the updated directive came into force.
"If the annex were adopted as it stands, wealthy private individuals would benefit from the system of exemption designed to benefit poor developing countries," the report said.
